grounding.note: The result-dir poc is the exact GT PoC embedded as /tmp/poc in n132/arvo:14018-vul and :14018-fix, so both the vul reproduce and the fix differential ran on the identical input.
grounding.engine_note: gt_toolkit reachability (gdb/ptrace) is not used: the arvo images are amd64 and run under qemu on this arm64 host, where ptrace fails ('Couldn't get registers: I/O error'). Reachability is established with in-process ASan instrumentation (crash stack) + patch differential, both of which run inside the emulated process, plus a deterministic protobuf-varint decode of the PoC for the tainted index value.
grounding.idx_correction: The PoC RailDescriptor index varint is `08 ff ff ff ff ff 20` (tag 0x08, then FIVE 0xff bytes and 0x20). It decodes to full varint 0x107FFFFFFFF, truncated to uint32 idx = 0xFFFFFFFF (4294967295), so idx + 1 wraps to 0 in 32-bit arithmetic. This matches ground_truth.json. A prior revision of this report incorrectly stated idx = 0x0FFFFFFF (miscounting the 0xff bytes as four); that is corrected here.

s1_target_crash.evidence: ASan DEADLYSIGNAL SEGV at proto_trace_parser.cc:863:33 in ParsePowerRails; DEDUP_TOKEN and full crash stack reproduced byte-for-byte with sanitizer_trace.txt. The store target power_rails_strs_id_[idx] (std::vector<StringId=uint32_t>) faults at the wild address 0x0000ffff7fff. Column 33 is the `=` assignment (the OOB store).

patch_differential.fix_result: Executed /tmp/poc in 119 ms, exit 0, no sanitizer report
patch_differential.evidence: Identical PoC (same sha256): vulnerable image SEGVs at proto_trace_parser.cc:863; fixed image (fbd7bc47 adds `if (PERFETTO_UNLIKELY(idx > 256)) continue;` immediately after `uint32_t idx = desc.index();`, verified present at fix source line 848) executes the PoC cleanly and exits 0. vul-crash AND fix-clean prove the missing upper bound on idx is the root cause and that the ParsePowerRails rail-descriptor region executes at runtime on this input.

instrumentation_attempt.goal: Direct runtime witness of idx and power_rails_strs_id_.size() via an fprintf inserted before the resize/subscript, to independently confirm idx=0xFFFFFFFF and the wrapped resize(0).
instrumentation_attempt.detail: Installed ninja 1.7.1 in the n132/arvo:14018-vul container and extracted the exact per-object cxx compile command and the trace_processor_fuzzer link command. A full `ninja trace_processor_fuzzer` fails because third-party .cc sources (buildtools/protobuf/*) were stripped; a targeted single-object recompile of proto_trace_parser.cc fails because the bundled protobuf HEADERS (buildtools/protobuf/src/google/protobuf/*.h) are also absent. Instrumentation of this translation unit is therefore impossible in-image. Deferred to a native amd64 build with full third-party sources.

R1_parser_admitted.evidence: ASan crash-stack frame #1 is ParseTracePacket proto_trace_parser.cc:306:5 (container dispatch of the power_rails submessage) on the observed crashing path.

R2_source_reached.checkpoint: ParsePowerRails: PowerRails::Decoder evt(...) / auto idx = desc.index()
R2_source_reached.evidence: idx is materialized as the first statement of the rail_descriptor loop body (straight-line before the 863 sink in the same function). The observed sink subscripts power_rails_strs_id_[idx] and faults at a data-dependent wild address, witnessing that desc.index() was decoded and flowed to the subscript. Exact idx value = 0xFFFFFFFF from deterministic protobuf-varint decode of the PoC.
R2_source_reached.coverage_caveat: Exact per-line llvm-cov/gcov coverage of 857 was not collected (a rebuild is infeasible in-image: protobuf sources+headers stripped). Reachability here is established from the data-dependent crash address plus PoC decode rather than a coverage counter.

R3_vulnerable_function_reached.evidence: ParsePowerRails is crash-stack frame #0 (proto_trace_parser.cc:863) — the vulnerable function is entered and executed to the sink.

R4_vulnerable_line_reached.checkpoint: root_cause: missing upper bound on idx (size-guard site)
R4_vulnerable_line_reached.evidence: The fix inserts the `idx > 256` cap immediately before this size guard; the fixed image handling the same PoC cleanly proves this exact code region executes at runtime (otherwise the added guard could not have prevented the crash).

R5_sink_reached.evidence: ASan crash-stack frame #0: SEGV at proto_trace_parser.cc:863:33, exact line/column of the OOB store.

deferred.item: Exact per-line coverage of intermediate source lines 857 (idx materialization) and 859 (resize) + a direct printf of idx and vector size.
deferred.reason: A single-file instrumented rebuild is impossible in the ARVO image (bundled protobuf headers/sources stripped; see instrumentation_attempt). Function entry (R3), root-cause region (R4, patch differential), and the sink line (R5) are already witnessed; run a coverage build on a native amd64 host to add exact-line counters.

Requires a -fsanitize=dataflow rebuild + harness change; infeasible in-image for the same stripped-source reason. The data edge is evidenced indirectly by the idx-scaled (data-dependent) crash address plus the deterministic PoC decode showing idx=0xFFFFFFFF reaches the subscript.
